# Florence 1347 – Economy & finance

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/europe-1347-florence.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Coinage (stamped metal money)** [`coinage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coinage.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The gold florin (1252) is Europe's standard, hammer-struck. Wages are paid in silver and black money. Silver is draining abroad, and the commune recoined the grosso in 1345 and 1347. Local: Zecca (mint); Arte del Cambio (money-changers). Elsewhere: Venice, the ducat; Genoa, the genovino.
- **Double-entry bookkeeping** [`double_entry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/double_entry.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Large Tuscan companies keep ledgers with matching debit and credit entries; layout and rigour vary, and small shops keep simple running accounts. No written manual exists. Local: ledgers of the merchant companies; abacus masters. Elsewhere: Genoa, communal treasury ledgers in full double entry (1340).
- **Interest-bearing loans, pledges and limits on debt bondage** [`interest_loans_collateral`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interest_loans_collateral.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Open interest is the sin of usury. Bankers hide it in exchange rates and 'gifts' on deposits; Christian pawnbrokers pay a yearly fine and repent in their wills. Local: Arte del Cambio; licensed pawnbrokers; friar confessors.
- **Deposit banking and bills of exchange** [`banking_credit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/banking_credit.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Deposits, book transfers and bills of exchange are routine. The Peruzzi (1343), Bardi (1346) and other houses have failed; depositors recover a fraction and credit is scarce. Local: Mercato Nuovo (bankers' tables); Arte del Cambio; Alberti and Strozzi companies; Francesco Pegolotti (Bardi factor). Elsewhere: Avignon, papal finances; Bruges and London, Italian exchange dealers.
- **Paper money** [`paper_money`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/paper_money.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Marco Polo describes the Khan's paper money, and Pegolotti tells merchants they must change silver for it in Cathay. After the bank failures nobody would trust a paper promise. Local: Pegolotti's Pratica della mercatura. Elsewhere: China, paper money under the Yuan (losing value).
- **Money supply, debasement and inflation** [`quantity_theory_inflation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quantity_theory_inflation.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Everyone knows that debased coin buys less and that good coin is hoarded or exported. That the amount of money moves all prices is not a stated idea. Elsewhere: France, the king's repeated changes of the coinage.
- **Risk-sharing partnership (commenda, mudaraba)** [`partnership_commenda`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/partnership_commenda.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Tuscan companies are partnerships renewed every few years, and every partner is liable with all he owns: the Bardi and Peruzzi partners are being stripped. Sea ventures use the commenda. Elsewhere: Genoa and Venice, commenda and colleganza.
- **Joint-stock company and limited liability** [`joint_stock_company`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/joint_stock_company.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. No company has tradable shares or limited liability. Transferable Monte credits are the nearest thing. Ruined partners would see the point at once. Elsewhere: Genoa, the Maona of Chios (shareholders of the 1346 fleet, founded 1347); Toulouse, shares in the river mills.
- **Insurance (marine, fire, life)** [`insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/insurance.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Sea risk is covered by sea loans or by carriers who charge for taking the risk. A contract for a premium alone is new: the oldest known is Genoese, 1347. Local: merchant companies shipping through Porto Pisano. Elsewhere: Genoa, notaries drawing the first premium contracts.
- **Life tables and the pricing of annuities** [`life_tables_annuities`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/life_tables_annuities.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Northern towns sell life rents at one price for all ages. No record of deaths by age exists; the baptistery counts only births. Elsewhere: Flemish and north French towns, life rents.
- **Public debt and government bonds** [`public_debt_bonds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_debt_bonds.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. In 1343–45 the commune, unable to repay its forced loans, made them the Monte Comune: transferable 5 % credits. They trade below face; friars debate whether buying them is usury. Local: Monte Comune; officials of the Monte. Elsewhere: Venice, the Monte (since 1262); Genoa, the compere.
- **Stock exchange (securities market)** [`stock_exchange`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/stock_exchange.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Brokers arrange exchange, goods and now Monte credits at the Mercato Nuovo. There are no fixed rules or posted prices. Local: Mercato Nuovo; brokers (sensali). Elsewhere: Bruges, merchants' exchange; Venice, Rialto.
- **Central bank and lender of last resort** [`central_bank`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/central_bank.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. No lender stood behind the failing banks; the commune itself was their debtor. The Monte manages debt, not credit. Elsewhere: Venice, Rialto transfer banks under state supervision.
- **Division of labour and specialisation** [`division_of_labour`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/division_of_labour.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Wool cloth passes through some two dozen trades under a merchant's direction; Villani counts over 200 workshops and 30,000 people living from it. Practised, never theorised. Local: Arte della Lana; Arte di Calimala (finishing imported cloth). Elsewhere: Venice, the Arsenal.
- **Comparative advantage and free trade** [`comparative_advantage_free_trade`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/comparative_advantage_free_trade.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Policy is protection and privilege: guild monopolies, tolls, grain export bans and wars over routes to the sea. Florence lives by importing English wool and exporting cloth.
- **Prices, supply and demand** [`price_mechanism_supply_demand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/price_mechanism_supply_demand.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Merchants and friars know prices follow scarcity; a grain dealer recorded Orsanmichele's prices for years. In the 1346–47 dearth the commune fixed prices and hunted hoarders. Local: grain market at Orsanmichele; grain officials of the commune.
- **Public granaries and price stabilisation (ever-normal granary)** [`ever_normal_granary`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ever_normal_granary.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. In dearth the commune appoints grain officials who buy abroad and sell or bake at a loss, as in 1346–47. A standing reserve is not kept. Local: grain officials (ufficiali del biado); Orsanmichele (grain market and store). Elsewhere: Venice, public grain office; China, ever-normal granaries.
- **Income tax and progressive rates** [`progressive_income_tax`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/progressive_income_tax.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept low. The city pays through gate and sales taxes and forced loans, which bear interest; the property assessment (estimo), dropped in 1315, is hated. Only the contado pays by assessed wealth. Local: gabelle offices; Monte Comune. Elsewhere: Siena, taxes on surveyed property.
- **Savings banks, credit and consumer cooperatives** [`cooperatives_savings_banks`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cooperatives_savings_banks.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Confraternities pool alms and guilds aid members. The poor borrow from pawnbrokers at high rates. No charitable pawn bank exists anywhere yet. Local: confraternities; Franciscans of Santa Croce.
- **Wealth as productivity; sustained economic growth** [`economic_growth_productivity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/economic_growth_productivity.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Wealth means treasure, land and the city's share of trade. Florentines see fortune's wheel in the bank failures; output per head rising for good is unimagined.
- **National income accounts (GDP)** [`national_accounts_gdp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/national_accounts_gdp.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Villani's chapter on Florence around 1338 counts mouths, cloths, shops, schools and communal revenue: the nearest thing in Europe. Households fear any count as a new tax. Local: Giovanni Villani; gabelle offices; guild matriculation lists.
- **Fighting slumps by sustaining demand (Keynesian policy)** [`aggregate_demand_countercyclical_policy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aggregate_demand_countercyclical_policy.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Money is coin, credit has collapsed and the commune cannot pay its own debts. Work on the cathedral and campanile to employ the poor is understood as piety and charity.
